findings.summary: §4 documented the SEAM blind spot but not the ATTRIBUTION one: a behavior exercised only by spawning a fresh process is unmeasurable by mutation on any tool, because no coverage tracer attributes child-process work to the parent test. Observed twice at 889 generated / 0 executed on a repo whose behavioral calls all shelled out (Codex 7e1f4539, fad338eb). §4a's killed+survived<generated rule DID catch it and correctly reported CANNOT MEASURE — the gap was doctrine on the remedy, so the documented response was to keep trying to make the tracer follow the child, which cannot work.
findings.disposition: §4 gains the attribution blind spot as a named second structural blindness beside the seam one, citing the two shas; §8 gains the remedy as a test-SHAPE rule — keep the fresh-process test (the real seam, and the only proof the executable runs and imports) and ADD an in-process twin driving the same public function, with the honest fallback of hand-applied targeted mutants plus an UNMEASURED label where no in-process seam exists. Latent in THIS repo: test_hooks.py:52 runs all 14 guard behaviors through subprocess.run, so any guard placed on a mutation roster would reproduce 889/0 exactly. Deliberately NOT fixed here — no mutation tool is configured anywhere in this repo (verified: no mutmut, no pyproject.toml/setup.cfg, no invocation in scripts/), so building twins would be ceremony for a gate that does not exist, and no debt was opened for the same reason.

findings.summary: §4a required baseline-green and explicitly said to check it "at HEAD", which is necessary but not sufficient: mutation tools run the suite against an instrumented REWRITTEN copy, and a suite green at HEAD can be red there, producing the identical generate-but-never-execute false green. That was Codex's first failure (889 mutants generated against a red rewritten-tree baseline). Compounding it, every §4a check was phrased "before trusting a pass", which invites running them post-hoc after the 40-minute pass is already spent.
findings.disposition: Baseline-green now explicitly means green in the tool's own rewritten tree AND at HEAD, named as two different facts in both places. Added a PREFLIGHT bullet reordering the checks §4a already required to run first — roster integrity including the duplicate-paths_to_mutate abort (mutmut 3.6 aborts after stats collection and names the cause nowhere), kill-test collection asserted as an exact count, rewritten-tree green, and a tracer-maps-at-least-one-function precheck that points at F1 when it maps none. Same assertions, seconds instead of a discarded hour. /mutate step 2 carries the operational form.

findings.summary: §12 instructs that absence claims about code must PARSE the code and assert on AST nodes rather than grep. Codex found that those exact tests are structurally unsatisfiable against a mutation tool's rewritten modules — so two of this Playbook's own correct rules collide, and the naive resolution (skip the module) silently drops the real kill tests sitting beside them.
findings.disposition: Named as a collision between two correct rules rather than a defect in either, in §4a beside the rewritten-tree precondition, with the resolution: register the individual TESTS in a mutation-only exclusion list, never their whole module. Also cited as the common cause when a suite is green at HEAD and red in the rewritten tree, so the diagnosis is attached to the symptom.

findings.summary: Three operational gaps the field report filed as Codex-specific runtime trivia, none of which are actually host-specific. §7 banned network but gave no rule for libraries that phone home by default (a Hugging Face retry loop was misread as a slow suite rather than a config failure) and no rule for sandbox refusals — a sandbox that blocks a loopback bind or a repo-local tool cache invites rewriting the assertion to fit it. §12 had no rule that a long run's evidence must outlive the session: a nearly complete full-suite run was lost to a context-compaction boundary, and the recovery instinct is to re-run the whole suite to reconstruct output already produced.
findings.disposition: Written HOST-NEUTRALLY into §7 and §12 rather than as the Codex addendum the report proposed — sandboxes, phone-home libraries and context compaction apply to every host, and SKILL.md vendors to both (install_into_repo.py:44), whereas a Codex-branded addendum would have landed in commands/ or agents/, both `unavailable` on Codex under the standing test-lock/codex-command-agent-discovery debt: dark on the exact host it was written for. §7 gains environment-restriction-never-weakens-a-test (move the artifact, not the assertion), offline-enforced-before-collection with a retry-loop-is-a-config-failure diagnostic, and hang-must-yield-a-stack. §12 gains evidence-you-cannot-re-read-is-not-evidence, which promotes what the release gate already practices. No new surface and no new debt on top of dated debt.

findings.summary: The span originally also updated agents/mutation-runner.md with the same preflight additions. agents/ is EFFECTFUL in the calibration ledger, so expect=none is unavailable there by construction, and the only corpus scenario covering that agent (shadowed-import-vacuous-suite) measures shadowed imports — a defect shape these preflight additions would not plausibly move. Registering expect=up against it to satisfy the coverage rule would have been exactly the instrument-satisfying the ledger's own rising no-effect share (16 of 63, 25%) warns about.
findings.disposition: The agent-brief edit was DROPPED from the commit rather than registered, and the reasoning is recorded in the L-20260817-01 ledger block so the omission is a visible decision instead of a gap. The brief change belongs with a plant+control pair authored for the child-process attribution shape, which is what §13 would require of it anyway. No dated debt opened: authoring corpus plants needs a live adversary model and human approval, and the brief is Claude-only in any case (agents are unavailable on Codex), so the deferral costs nothing that is currently reachable.
